Hank / Sumeet —

Quick handoff from Sales to the Implementation squad. Congratulations on getting to the migration phase — our goal is a low-risk cutover with predictable RPS and no user-visible regressions. Attached are the code bundle and a lightweight runbook to get started.

High-level plan (proposed):
- Week 0: Tech-intake call (45m) to validate integration scope and traffic pattern.
- Week 1: Sandbox setup + SDK sample integration (Node/Python) and one smoke test.
- Week 2: Staged cutover (blue/green) + traffic shaping and latency SLO validation.
- Week 3: Full cutover + 24h observation window; rollback plan ready.

Key technical notes for the team:
- SDK setup: our SDKs are backwards-compatible with your current client; prefer the 1.x migration shim in the examples.
- Endpoint migration: use the endpoint-mapping table in the runbook; traffic shift should be in 10% increments with 15–30 minute observation windows.
- Retries/timeouts: we recommend exponential backoff (initial 250ms, max 5s) for transient 5xx and 429 responses; see retry matrix.
- Rate limits: we included a suggested token-based rate-limit matrix (rate-limit-matrix.csv) tuned to your peak traffic estimate.

Next steps / asks for Fintech Labs:
1) Confirm a 45-minute slot for the kick-off this week (I put a few optional times below).
2) Share the sandbox API key or a read-only sample token for our dev team.
3) Tell us if you require SOC2 evidence — we can loop in Security.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-examples.zip (zip), integration-runbook-v1.2.pdf (pdf), rate-limit-matrix.csv (csv)

Hi Hank / team — Naomi from Implementation here. Short answers + concrete patterns below.

1) Idempotency & webhooks
- SDK support: the Node and Python SDKs include a helper for idempotency (Idempotency-Key header generator) and we recommend storing request_id/server_nonce in your gateway. The SDK attaches a checksum header X-Redwood-Body-Hash by default.
- Webhook pattern: persist webhook events with a unique event_id; if you must retry delivery, use at-least-once semantics but design the consumer as idempotent (event dedupe key). Example snippet in the runbook.

2) Retries/timeouts (recommended configuration)
- Client timeout: 8s overall per request (includes connect + response).
- Retries: exponential backoff with jitter: retry delays = min(500ms * 2^n, 5000ms) + random up to 200ms. Max retries = 4 for idempotent GET/HEAD; 2 for POSTs with Idempotency-Key.
- Circuit breaker: open after 20 consecutive 5xx responses for a given endpoint for 60s.

Example (Node):
const client = new RedwoodSDK({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, timeout: 8000, retries: 4 });
// basic request with idempotency
await client.requests.create({ data }, { idempotencyKey: 'invoice-12345' });

cURL (timeout + retry example):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: invoice-12345" \
  --max-time 8 \
  --retry 3 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 1

3) Cutover & rollback
- Blue/Green approach: route traffic to green in 10% increments over 2 hours outside your peak window. Each step: ramp 10% -> 15–30 min observation (latency, error rate, cost). If errors spike > 2.5x baseline we rollback.
- Quick rollback: routing changes are atomic at our edge; a rollback is a single config flip and should take < 60s to enforce globally. The observation windows are the longer part.

4) Rate limiting behaviors
- Soft-throttle: supported. Our gateway can return 429 with Retry-After header and push metrics to your dashboard. We recommend client-side leaky-bucket smoothing and an exponential backoff on 429s.

5) Sandbox keys & observability
- Please send a sandbox token (revocable). We'll attach a temporary tracing tag so you can see representative spans and token-level metrics in Console.

I've also added a short checklist at the top of the runbook for quick wins (smoke test, schema validation, rollout gates). See attached runbook and code bundle.

Let me know which kickoff slot works and we'll send an invite with the technical agenda.

—
